input.text: Beside the railway station stands something remarkable: the last living piece of Beijing's medieval city wall. For five centuries, a wall of rammed earth and brick, with gates and towers, enclosed the Ming capital. When the city modernized, nearly all of it came down — but this section survived, and the park before you preserves it as a quiet, climbable ruin. At its east end rises the Corner Tower — a vast two-roofed watchtower from the fourteen hundreds, one of the largest surviving watchtowers of any Chinese city wall — its arrow slits still staring down the tracks where the trains now run. Inside the tower, a small museum shows old Beijing's gates and defenses. In early spring, the plum garden below blooms into the city's favorite flower scene. Walk the wall's grassy base at dusk — Beijing, five hundred years ago and five hundred meters from the subway.
